vis.alt: Table of four hypoxia types: hypoxic with low PaO2 such as altitude, anaemic with normal PaO2 but low oxygen content, stagnant with normal PaO2 and low flow as in shock, histotoxic with normal PaO2 where cells cannot use oxygen as in cyanide poisoning.
vis.caption: Only hypoxic hypoxia has a low PaO2; the other three have normal PaO2, so pulse oximetry can mislead.

vis.alt: Table of high altitude illness: acute mountain sickness with headache and nausea treated by rest and acetazolamide, high altitude cerebral oedema with ataxia and confusion treated by descent and dexamethasone, high altitude pulmonary oedema with dyspnoea and crackles treated by descent and nifedipine.
vis.caption: Descent is definitive for all three; acetazolamide prevents AMS, dexamethasone treats HACE, nifedipine treats HAPE.
